newsitem.title: USA: Piper Jaffray litigation settlement okayed.
newsitem.headline: Piper Jaffray litigation settlement okayed.

text.p: Piper Jaffray Cos Inc said Wednesday that the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington at Seattle granted preliminary approval for a $15.5 million settlement agreement in closed-end fund litigation.

The court set a final hearing date of June 23, 1997 for approval of the agreement, which was publicly announced in June 1996. The terms of the settlement include a payment by Piper Jaffray of $15.5 million over a four-year period and share repurchase offers.

The agreement affects American Government Income Fund Inc, American Government Income Portfolio Inc, American Opportunity Income Fund Inc, American Government Term Trust, American Strategic Income Portfolio Inc Portfolios I, II and III, and American Select Portfolio Inc.
The repurchase offers exclude American Government Term Trust, which was liquidated in 1995.
The class action includes shareholders who purchased or otherwise acquired shares from April 21, 1988, through and including May 1, 1995.
Based on the final hearing date, Piper Jaffray said it estimates that the earliest mailing of share repurchase offers would be in September 1997.

In addition, as part of the settlement, the fund boards will propose conversion of American Government Income Fund, American Government Income Portfolio and American Opportunity Income Fund to an open-end format in approximately two years. That would be based on certain conditions being met and the board determining that conversion would be in the shareholders' best interest.
